title: 11th Word: Introduction to the Parable and the Sultan's Purpose

questions.question: What is the main thing the reader is invited to understand through the comparison in this passage?
questions.answer: The comparison is meant to help explain the purpose of the world, why human beings were created, and the mystery of the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: What kind of person is described in the comparison, and what does he possess?
questions.answer: It describes a king who has enormous wealth, hidden treasures, advanced skills, broad knowledge, and deep learning.

questions.question: Besides material wealth, what other forms of excellence does the king have?
questions.answer: He also has mastery in arts, knowledge of many sciences, and wide learning in difficult fields.

questions.question: Why does the king want to establish an exhibition?
questions.answer: He wants to display his rule, wealth, art, and knowledge, and also to witness his own beauty and perfection.

questions.question: According to the passage, what general tendency is attributed to anyone who has beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: Such a person naturally wants to see and show that beauty and perfection.

questions.question: What is the first of the two ways the king wants to behold his beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: He wants to see it directly with his own discerning awareness.

questions.question: What is the second way the king wants to behold his beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: He wants to see it reflected in the perception of others.

questions.question: What does the mention of hidden treasures suggest about the king?
questions.answer: It suggests that his riches are not limited to what is obvious and that he possesses deeper wonders not immediately seen.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the king’s inner qualities with his outward display?
questions.answer: His inner excellences, like knowledge and skill, lead him to make them visible through a public display.

questions.question: Why is the reader told to consider the comparison together with the speaker’s own nafs?
questions.answer: It points to a personal and reflective approach, showing that understanding these truths also involves examining oneself.

questions.question: What three major themes are named at the start as needing explanation?
questions.answer: The purpose of the world, the creation of human beings, and the reality of the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: What method is used to explain those themes?
questions.answer: They are explained through a brief illustrative comparison.

questions.question: How is the king’s wealth described?
questions.answer: His wealth includes many treasure stores filled with precious stones and other valuable things.

questions.question: What is added to the description of the king’s treasures besides the visible riches?
questions.answer: There are also concealed stores that are extraordinary and marvelous.

questions.question: How is the king’s intellectual and artistic ability presented?
questions.answer: He is shown as highly accomplished in unusual arts and deeply knowledgeable in many sciences and forms of learning.

questions.question: What motivates the king to create a place of display?
questions.answer: His desire to make his beauty and perfection known and visible motivates him.

questions.question: What specific things does he want people to see in that display?
questions.answer: He wants them to see the grandeur of his authority, the brilliance of his wealth, the excellence of his craftsmanship, and the wonders of his knowledge.

questions.question: In what two directions does the king seek to behold his own perfection?
questions.answer: One is directly by himself, and the other is through the sight and appreciation of others.

questions.question: What tone does the passage use when addressing the reader at the beginning?
questions.answer: It uses a direct, personal, and instructive tone, as if guiding a close companion.

questions.question: What does the passage ask the reader to do in order to grasp the ideas being discussed?
questions.answer: It asks the reader to reflect on a short comparison.

questions.question: Who is the central figure in that comparison?
questions.answer: The central figure is a king.

questions.question: What does the king own that shows his outward riches?
questions.answer: He owns many stores of jewels and other precious valuables.

questions.question: What does the passage say about treasures that are not openly visible?
questions.answer: It says the king also has hidden treasures that are wondrous.

questions.question: What abilities show that the king’s greatness is not only financial?
questions.answer: His skill in arts, his knowledge of many sciences, and his deep learning show that.

questions.question: What does the king decide to open, and for what basic reason?
questions.answer: He decides to open an exhibition so his qualities can be made known and displayed.

questions.question: Which aspects of the king are meant to become visible to people through this exhibition?
questions.answer: His sovereignty, riches, artistic excellence, and knowledge are meant to become visible.

questions.question: What is the first stated purpose in the king’s seeing his own beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: The first purpose is his own direct awareness and observation of them.

questions.question: What is the second stated purpose?
questions.answer: The second purpose is to observe them through the viewpoint of others.

questions.question: According to the opening of the passage, what subjects is the comparison supposed to illuminate?
questions.answer: It is supposed to illuminate the world’s purpose, human creation, and the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: What does the speaker include along with the comparison, and what does that suggest?
questions.answer: The speaker includes his own nafs, suggesting self-examination is part of understanding the lesson.

questions.question: What sort of resources does the king have in terms of wealth?
questions.answer: He has many treasure houses filled with rare and precious items.

questions.question: How does the passage distinguish between the king’s visible and hidden possessions?
questions.answer: It mentions both obvious stores of wealth and separate concealed treasures.

questions.question: What kinds of non-material strengths belong to the king?
questions.answer: He has artistic mastery, comprehensive scientific knowledge, and extensive scholarship.

questions.question: What desire is said to belong to every possessor of beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: Such a possessor wants both to witness and to show that beauty and perfection.

questions.question: How does that general principle help explain the king’s actions?
questions.answer: It explains why he wants to prepare a public setting where his excellences can be displayed.

questions.question: What does the king want to manifest before people?
questions.answer: He wants to make apparent the greatness of his rule, the sparkle of his wealth, the wonders of his craftsmanship, and the marvels of his learning.

questions.question: What is meant by the king beholding his perfection with his own discerning eye?
questions.answer: It means he directly contemplates and appreciates his own qualities.

questions.question: What is meant by his beholding it through the view of others?
questions.answer: It means he sees those qualities reflected in how others notice and respond to them.

questions.question: What is introduced after the quoted verses?
questions.answer: A comparison is introduced to help explain major truths about existence, humanity, and worship.

questions.question: How is the intended explanation described in terms of size or scope?
questions.answer: It is described as a small or brief comparison.

questions.question: What does the king possess that points to luxury and abundance?
questions.answer: He possesses many treasures full of highly valuable gems and other riches.

questions.question: What phrase in the passage shows that the king’s wealth is not fully exhausted by those riches?
questions.answer: The passage adds that he has additional hidden stores beyond the visible treasures.

questions.question: In what areas is the king highly accomplished besides owning wealth?
questions.answer: He excels in unusual arts, numerous sciences, and many difficult branches of learning.

questions.question: What common human tendency is used to explain the king’s motive?
questions.answer: The passage says that one who has beauty and perfection wants to see it and show it.

questions.question: What action does the king take because of that motive?
questions.answer: He wants to prepare an exhibition and arrange displays in it.

questions.question: For whose benefit is the display arranged?
questions.answer: It is arranged both for the people to observe and for the king himself to behold his own perfection.

questions.question: What are the two distinct perspectives from which the king wants to see his beauty?
questions.answer: One is his own direct perception, and the other is the perception of others.

questions.question: How does the beginning address to “Brother” shape the feel of the passage?
questions.answer: It makes the tone warm, personal, and advisory rather than distant or purely abstract.

questions.question: What is the reader told he may come to understand by reflecting on the comparison?
questions.answer: He may come to understand something about the meaning of the world, the reason for human creation, and the mystery of formal prayer.

questions.question: What personal element is included in the act of reflection?
questions.answer: The speaker mentions reflecting together with his own self or nafs.

questions.question: Who appears in the story, and what is his social position?
questions.answer: A king appears, and he is presented as a ruler of great rank.

questions.question: What details show the scale of the king’s riches?
questions.answer: He owns numerous treasure stores filled with precious gems and other valuables.

questions.question: What extra detail deepens the picture of his wealth?
questions.answer: The passage says he has further hidden treasures that are remarkable.

questions.question: How does the text portray the king’s mental and practical abilities?
questions.answer: It portrays him as highly skilled, broadly knowledgeable, and deeply learned.

questions.question: What does the king want to make visible through an exhibition?
questions.answer: He wants to make visible his majesty, wealth, artistic achievement, and knowledge.

questions.question: Why is the desire to display these things presented as natural?
questions.answer: Because the passage treats the wish to witness and reveal beauty and perfection as fitting for anyone who possesses them.

questions.question: What is one way the king wants to witness his own perfection?
questions.answer: He wants to witness it directly by himself.

questions.question: What is the other way?
questions.answer: He wants to witness it through how others see it.
